name: iter2-screens
description: Round 2 MAP screens on equal_prior_concepts_with_guess_lapse (NLL 904.5): new concept families and response tweaks gain at most ~1.8 nats
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 2, candidate_4 (2026-10-30). Baseline in-sample NLL 904.5. Adding decade, repdigit, digit-sum, single-digit or "contains both digits" rules gave no gain. Logit sharpening gave 0. Free example noise gave 902.7, but lapse then drops to about 0.008, so it would duplicate `digit_concepts_inferred_outlier_rate`. A rule prior proportional to |rule|^gamma gave 903.3 with gamma≈-0.24, a slight preference for narrow rules. I submitted that as `rule_breadth_prior_concepts`. Its smoke loglik was -904.8 and the fit took about 2 s per 200 iterations.

**Why:** this confirms [[number-game-ceiling]]. Most of the residual is 5-response-per-cell binomial noise.
**How to apply:** don't re-screen these concept families. Further gains are unlikely without participant-level structure, and the CSV has no participant column.

Round 2 cand_5 repair (2026-10-30): `specificity_biased_rule_prior_lapse` was rejected as a near-duplicate of `rule_breadth_prior_concepts` (RMSE 0.0003). The repair is `occam_specificity_prior_all_concepts`, which applies the same |c|^-g to intervals too, normalised within each class and collapsed to 100 size groups per set. Smoke loglik was -904.4, about 16 s per 200 iterations. Applying g to intervals moves p_yes by RMSE ≈ 0.01 at g = 0.1, which clears the 0.002 novelty gate.

name: fit-speed-budget
description: Admission fit is 7000 iters/chain warm-start NUTS; per-gradient cost must be ~<25ms; tricks that worked
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1d82c78b-0bac-4618-97c8-da7bd32baa1b
  modified: 2026-10-30T21:06:41.047Z
---

Admission fits use production draws 4000 + tune 3000 per chain (warm_start_nuts, dense mass matrix), 30-min limit per run. Machine has 1 core. Incumbent `tenenbaum_digit_concepts` logp+grad ≈ 12 ms. A memory-subset mixture over its hypothesis space (≈700 states) cost 62 ms naive → too slow (~49 min).

**Why:** the check_candidate smoke fit (200 iters) passes even when the full fit would time out.

**How to apply:** benchmark logp+dlogp time and NUTS n_steps (probe `_warm_start_sample` with small draws) before finishing. Speedups that worked: replace gathering posterior rows per cell (slow AdvancedIncSubtensor1 gradient) with a `pytensor.sparse.CSR` + `structured_dot` (44→25 ms); declaring module-level `SAMPLER_SETTINGS = {"target_accept": 0.9}` halves steps (10.8→5.3). Don't name a scratch script `timeit.py` (shadows stdlib, breaks pymc import). Related: [[digit-concepts-key]].

Also worked (2026-10-30, `order_weighted_concept_learning`): when intervals must be grouped by (size, per-position hit pattern) instead of (size, k), keep only each set's non-empty groups (≤473 of 1600 on this data) padded per set, and gather size-dependent terms by index — 47 → 18 ms.
---
name: number-game-ceiling
description: Rule+interval+digit concept model is near its ceiling; single-param tweaks gain only 3-6 nats in-sample
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 1 (iter_1, candidate_5) MAP screens with equal-weight 44-rule + uniform-interval model (in-sample NLL 912): free example-noise 908.5, lapse 907.9, noise+lapse 906.3, logit response map 908.6, size-principle exponent 911.6, Erlang interval prior 913.5 (uniform is better), rule-family weights about 911, free 45 weights 893 (but the extra params cost it on LOO). Calibration by predicted-p bin is already good. Biggest per-set residuals: 83,38,58,68 (scattered 20-40% yes in the 50s-70s), 85,19,91 (odd numbers overpredicted), 14,47.
Submitted `equal_prior_concepts_with_guess_lapse` (the lapse model with one shared rule prior): smoke loglik -905.8.

**Why:** the next improvement probably needs a new mechanism, not another response or prior parameter. Builds on [[digit-concepts-key]].
**How to apply:** don't spend rounds on noise/lapse/exponent tweaks; look at the residual sets above.

Round 2 cand_5 (2026-10-30) numpy MAP screens on the incumbent (NLL 904.5): strong/weak sampling mix 904.5 (no gain), bonus for round-boundary (decade) intervals 904.5, lapse drifting with trial_index 904.3, guess-yes drift 904.5, rule prior ∝ size^-g 903.3 (g≈0.25), all-hypothesis prior ∝ size^-g 902.7. Submitted `specificity_biased_rule_prior_lapse` (rule-only version, smoke loglik -904.7). Data = 5 sessions × 450 trials, contiguous in the CSV (trial_index resets), n=5 per cell, so most residual is binomial noise. Reusable screener: a numpy set × hypothesis log-lik matrix with Nelder-Mead runs in about 1 min per variant.

examples drawn uniformly), plus a response lapse -- on a fraction `lapse` of
trials the participant ignores the concept and answers "yes" with probability
`guess_yes`. The one change: no learned preference among rules. All 45 rules
share the rule prior lambda_0 equally, instead of 45 separately inferred
weights; each interval keeps prior (1 - lambda_0) / 5050.
"""

import pymc as pm

NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)

    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return list(rules.values())

INTERVALS = [list(range(m, n + 1)) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)]

# Size-principle log P(x | h) of one example: the teacher's model of the learner.
BASE_LOG_LIK = np.log(ALPHA * MEMBERSHIP / MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True) + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)
RULE_LOG_MARGINAL = logsumexp(BASE_LOG_LIK[:N_RULES], axis=0)  # (100,) log sum_r P(x | r)
INTERVAL_LOG_MARGINAL = logsumexp(BASE_LOG_LIK[N_RULES:], axis=0)  # (100,)

SAMPLER_SETTINGS = {"target_accept": 0.9}

with pm.Model() as model:
    # (sets, 100) counts of each number among a set's examples, as sparse CSR parts.
    count_data = pm.Data("count_data", np.ones(1))
    count_indices = pm.Data("count_indices", np.zeros(1, dtype="int32"))
    count_indptr = pm.Data("count_indptr", np.array([0, 1], dtype="int32"))
    n_sets = pm.Data("n_sets", np.ones(1, dtype="int64"))
    example_counts = pytensor.sparse.CSR(count_data, count_indices, count_indptr, pt.stack([n_sets[0], 100]))
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # set index * 100 + target - 1
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    lambda_0 = pm.Beta("lambda_0", 2, 2)
    teach = pm.HalfNormal("teach", sigma=1.0)  # strength of the helpful-teacher assumption
    log_prior_rule = pt.log(lambda_0) - np.log(N_RULES)
    log_prior_interval = pt.log1p(-lambda_0) - np.log(N_INTERVALS)

    # Learner's marginal P(x); the teacher favours members x with small P(x).
    log_z = pt.logaddexp(log_prior_rule + RULE_LOG_MARGINAL, log_prior_interval + INTERVAL_LOG_MARGINAL)
    log_u = -teach * log_z
    u = pt.exp(log_u - pt.max(log_u))  # (100,)
    cum_u = pt.concatenate([pt.zeros(1), pt.cumsum(u)])
    norm = pt.concatenate([pt.dot(RULE_MEMBERSHIP, u), cum_u[INTERVAL_HI] - cum_u[INTERVAL_LO - 1]])  # (H,)

    # Teacher log-likelihood gain of example x under each concept containing
    # it, over the 10% random-number floor; summed over each set's examples.
    gain = MEMBERSHIP.T * (pt.log(ALPHA * u[:, None] / norm[None, :] + (1 - ALPHA) / 100) - np.log((1 - ALPHA) / 100))
    log_lik = pytensor.sparse.structured_dot(example_counts, gain)  # (sets, H), up to a per-set constant
    log_prior = pt.concatenate([pt.repeat(log_prior_rule, N_RULES), pt.repeat(log_prior_interval, N_INTERVALS)])
    posterior = pt.special.softmax(log_lik + log_prior[None, :], axis=1)
    in_concept = pt.dot(posterior, MEMBERSHIP)  # (sets, 100)

    p_concept = pt.clip(in_concept.reshape((-1,))[row_cell], 0.0, 1.0)
    lapse = pm.Beta("lapse", 2, 8)
    guess_yes = pm.Beta("guess_yes", 2, 2)
    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip((1 - lapse) * p_concept + lapse * guess_yes, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))

def _warm_start_sample(model: Any, settings: Dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
    """NUTS started from the posterior mode (``fit.method: warm_start_nuts``).

    The mode of the unconstrained log density (Jacobians in) by L-BFGS-B, the
    Hessian there by central differences of the gradient, then NUTS with the
    inverse Hessian as a fixed dense mass matrix and each chain started at a
    draw of N(mode, H^-1); tuning adapts only the step size. The draws are NUTS
    draws, judged by the same gate as any fit. On the number game's seeds a fit
    took ~30 s at tune 200 / draws 250 where production NUTS took ~25 min. A
    Hessian that is not positive definite (a direction neither data nor prior
    pins down) has no metric: the fit fails, as the model's own failure.
    """
    from pymc.blocking import DictToArrayBijection, RaveledVars
    from pymc.step_methods.hmc.integration import CpuLeapfrogIntegrator
    from pymc.step_methods.hmc.quadpotential import QuadPotentialFull
    from scipy.optimize import minimize

    pm = _import_pymc()
    with model:
        step = pm.NUTS(target_accept=settings["target_accept"], max_treedepth=settings["max_treedepth"])
    # The step's own compiled log density and gradient (Jacobians in), on the
    # raveled continuous parameters: no second compile for the optimizer.
    logp_dlogp = step._logp_dlogp_func
    logp_dlogp.set_extra_values({})
    start = model.initial_point(random_seed=settings["random_seed"])
    x0 = DictToArrayBijection.map({v.name: start[v.name] for v in step.vars})
    grad = lambda x: np.asarray(logp_dlogp(x)[1], dtype=float)  # noqa: E731
    mode = minimize(lambda x: -float(logp_dlogp(x)[0]), x0.data, jac=lambda x: -grad(x), method="L-BFGS-B").x
    h = 1e-5
    hessian = np.array([(grad(mode + h * e) - grad(mode - h * e)) / (2 * h) for e in np.eye(mode.size)])
    precision = -(hessian + hessian.T) / 2
    try:
        chol = np.linalg.cholesky(precision)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "warm-start NUTS: the Hessian at the posterior mode is not positive definite (some "
            "parameter direction is pinned down by neither the data nor the prior)"
        ) from None
    # The integrator holds the potential it was built with.
    step.potential = QuadPotentialFull(np.linalg.inv(precision))
    step.integrator = CpuLeapfrogIntegrator(step.potential, logp_dlogp)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(settings["random_seed"])
    starts = mode + np.linalg.solve(chol.T, rng.standard_normal((settings["chains"], mode.size)).T).T
    free = [v for v in model.unobserved_value_vars if v.name in {rv.name for rv in model.free_RVs}]
    free_values = model.compile_fn(inputs=model.value_vars, outs=free)

    def point(x: np.ndarray) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
        return {**start, **DictToArrayBijection.rmap(RaveledVars(x, x0.point_map_info))}

    with model:
        idata = pm.sample(
            draws=settings["draws"], tune=settings["tune"], chains=settings["chains"], cores=settings["cores"],
            step=step, initvals=[dict(zip([v.name for v in free], free_values(point(x)))) for x in starts],
            progressbar=False, random_seed=settings["random_seed"], idata_kwargs={"log_likelihood": True},
        )
    idata.posterior.attrs["fit_method"] = "warm_start_nuts"
    return idata


def write_fit_file(idata: Any, nc_path: Path) -> None:
    """Persist ``idata`` at ``nc_path`` atomically.

    The fit is written to a temporary file beside ``nc_path`` and renamed into
    place, so a process killed mid-write (an out-of-memory kill, a time limit)
    leaves no ``.nc`` at all rather than a truncated one that every later run
    would find in the cache. The temporary name does not end in ``.nc``.
    """
    nc_path = Path(nc_path)
    partial = nc_path.with_name(f".{nc_path.name}.{os.getpid()}.partial")
    try:
        idata.to_netcdf(str(partial))
        os.replace(partial, nc_path)
    finally:
        partial.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    """Persist ``idata`` at ``nc_path`` atomically.

    leaves no ``.nc`` at all rather than a truncated one that every later run
    would find in the cache. The temporary name does not end in ``.nc``.

teacher, not drawn at random from the concept. The teacher picks, among the
concept's members, numbers that would most lead a learner to that concept --
P_teach(x | h) is proportional to P(h | x)^teach over the members x of h, where
P(h | x) is a size-principle learner's belief after seeing x alone -- and the
participant infers the concept by inverting this teacher. Hypotheses: the 45
arithmetic and digit rules (equal rule prior lambda_0) and every interval of
1..100, 10% of examples random, plus a guess lapse (rates of guessed yes and
guessed no). teach = 0 recovers the size principle; teach > 0 makes examples
that few concepts contain more diagnostic.

The teacher's imagined learner splits its prior evenly between rules and
intervals. Because single-example likelihoods are constant within a concept,
P(h | x)^teach over members reduces to u_x = Z_x^-teach, Z_x the imagined
learner's marginal probability of x. Each set's (and each set-target cell's)
summed rule and interval likelihoods then depend on teach alone; they are
tabulated per stimulus in prepare_observed as Chebyshev series in teach
(log scale), and lambda_0 enters exactly.

import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt

ALPHA = 0.9
FLOOR = (1 - ALPHA) / 100
NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)
TEACH_MAX = 3.0  # series domain [0, TEACH_MAX]; the prior puts < 1e-6 beyond it

        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return list(rules.values())

INTERVALS = [list(range(m, n + 1)) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)]

    """Rows carry `number_set` ("16,8", in presented order), `target` and `rating`."""
    sets = [tuple(int(x) for x in str(r["number_set"]).split(",")) for r in rows]
    unique = list(dict.fromkeys(sets))
    set_index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(unique)}
    cells = list(dict.fromkeys((s, int(r["target"])) for s, r in zip(sets, rows)))
    cell_index = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(cells)}
    cell_s = np.array([set_index[s] for s, _ in cells], dtype="int64")
    cell_t = np.array([t - 1 for _, t in cells], dtype="int64")
    counts = np.zeros((len(unique), 100))
    for i, s in enumerate(unique):
        for x in s:
            counts[i, x - 1] += 1

        "set_rule_coef": fit(at_nodes[0]),
        "cell_rule_coef": fit(at_nodes[1]),
        "set_interval_coef": fit(at_nodes[2]),
        "cell_interval_coef": fit(at_nodes[3]),
        "cell_set": cell_s,
        "row_cell": np.array([cell_index[(s, int(r["target"]))] for s, r in zip(sets, rows)], dtype="int64"),
        "rating": np.array([int(r["rating"]) for r in rows], dtype="int64"),
    }

I've submitted `pedagogical_sampling_concepts`, and the admission check prints `OK` (smoke-fit log-likelihood -906.4). On this data it only ties the incumbent: it doesn't fix anything, and the critique found no significant discrepancies to target.

**Hypothesis:** people assume a helpful teacher chose the examples, rather than the program drawing them at random from the concept. The teacher is assumed to pick members of the concept that would best point a learner to it, meaning numbers that few other plausible concepts contain. People then infer the concept by reasoning about why these particular examples were picked. This is a social, communicative inference process, which no model in the set has. It uses the same rules, digit concepts, numeric ranges and guessing as the base model. One new parameter (`teach`) sets how strongly they hold the teacher assumption; at 0 the model reduces exactly to the equal-prior lapse model.

**What I tried first.** Quick fits of the best settings against the base model (in-sample error 904.5) for four process ideas:
- **Forgetting some examples:** the fitted forgetting rate went to 0.
- **Carry-over from the previous trial** (its set or its target): no effect.
- **A compressed (logarithmic) mental number line for ranges:** clearly worse, about 19 nats.
- **Helpful teacher:** fitted strength about 0.05–0.2, gaining at most 0.1 nats. I picked this one because it is the most distinct mechanism, not because it fits better.

**Novelty and speed:**
- **Novelty:** at the short fit's posterior mean (`teach` ≈ 0.19), its predictions on the novelty pool differ from the base model's by RMSE about 0.005. That clears the 0.002 duplicate threshold. If the full fit puts `teach` lower (around 0.1 or less), it could fall close to that line.
- **Speed:** a direct version took 171 ms per gradient, too slow for the 30-minute limit. To fix that, two simplifications are built into the model:
  - The teacher's imagined learner splits its prior evenly between rules and ranges, instead of using the participant's own fitted split.
  - Each set's rule and range likelihoods are precomputed as smooth functions of `teach`, accurate to about 1e-10.

  It now takes 0.3 ms per gradient, about 6.5 sampler steps per iteration, with no divergences in a 500-iteration warm-start probe. One small change from the base model: the guessing is parameterized as separate "guessed yes" and "guessed no" rates, to give the sampler a cleaner posterior shape.

I also saved these screen results and the speed-up method to the memory notes (`iter3-process-screens.md`).

Files are in `iter_3/candidate_2/`:
- `hypothesis.md`
- `model_name.txt`
- `candidate.py`
